description: The second series pushes harder on transformations, sequences and visual misdirection, with the strongest questions rewarding contestants who stop calculating and notice the simpler structural rule hidden in the wording.

s02e01.description: A painting makes a wristwatch look like a bangle, a chessboard and letter-building puzzles test visual attention, and adding letters produces BOAT, PLANE, TRAIN and SHIP. The common connection, and the episode's neatest reveal, is FORMS OF TRANSPORT.

s02e02.description: The ladder moves through a bees-knees expression puzzle and a rhyme set built around LABEL, TABLE and STABLE. A penultimate question resolves to five, leaving a compact mixture of language and number logic before the final one-percent test.

s02e03.description: A calendar puzzle asks which month names contain three vowels, TWELVE is rearranged with an added letter, and animal names hide inside ordinary words. The final asks for the hundredth digit written when positive integers are listed in order, landing on the first digit of 55: five.

s02e04.description: Playing-card logic, a puzzle involving trees and a twelve-item sequence all appear before the final clue is recognized as the months of the year. The missing item is not another month but the common ending required by the sequence: the letter E.

s02e05.description: British notes and coins must be combined to total exactly £88.88, while another question tracks vowels through month names. The final depends on hearing number words rather than merely seeing them, using embedded number sounds as the route through the puzzle.

s02e06.description: A Roman figure wearing modern trainers starts the visual misdirection, with number sequences, credit-card digits and flags following. The final compares rows of month days and hinges on the exceptional twenty-ninth day, revealing the leap-year rule.

s02e07.description: Short verbal traps include a four-letter answer, POST, and a question where the relationship between four and five matters more than arithmetic. Later puzzles mix diagonal multiplication and opposites before the last missing-word problem demands another switch of interpretation.

s02e08.description: A word puzzle builds a CIRCLE OF TRUST, blue is examined simply as a four-letter word and a field of arrows asks which one does not point toward another arrow. Even the days of the week become a trap before the finalists face the one-percent question.
